subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should deferred context-engine maintenance permanently use this new disabled-by-default setting and host-owned fence, or should it use a canonical existing timeout and cancellation policy instead?
rationale: The choices differ in default user behavior, config growth, plugin expectations, and shutdown/session ownership; code correctness alone cannot establish the intended product contract.

options.title: Approve opt-in host fence
options.body: Land the disabled-by-default setting and host-owned fence/persistence barrier as the compatibility-preserving contract.

options.title: Choose a finite default
options.body: Keep the mechanism but select a finite default that automatically fixes the stall, with upgrade proof for legitimately long maintenance runs.

options.title: Consolidate timeout policy
options.body: Replace the new setting with a maintainer-selected existing compaction or session safety budget and document the coupled semantics.

recommendation.title: Approve opt-in host fence
recommendation.body: Land the disabled-by-default setting and host-owned fence/persistence barrier as the compatibility-preserving contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision centers on the context-engine lifecycle and plugin/runtime ownership boundary represented in prior merged work.
